The rule or link is downgraded.
The model never queries the database;
In ⑦, what moves one metric is scattered over
many rows. One page gathers and ranks it.
Each number is checked against its
Organized by metric: each page covers one metric. It lists the parameters that moved it, with direction
and grade, ranked by grade: High confidence first.
Organized by parameter: each page covers one parameter. It lists every final metric it moved,
with direction and grade, side effects included.
Organized by experiment: the model writes a chain of intermediate metrics that explains the result.
Every link is then checked against the data.
Method: causal discovery (PC / GES in causal-learn), one row per experiment: which metric is upstream?
Stronger than usual: each row is a randomized test, rules restrict the graph, Check verifies each link.
Knowledge, no advice: for one business area, the parameters that help or hurt each key metric,
a list to recommend, a list to avoid, and the key metrics that still have no reliable lever.
One page per series: the same parameter tested again and again. How many rounds brought new
information, how many only repeated earlier ones? Is this line still worth continuing?
One page per cluster of similar changes. Changes in a cluster tend to act alike, so a tested one is
used to guess an untested one. Each cluster is checked by hiding one member and predicting it.
Advice, unlike the domain page: for one goal, e.g. “raise clicks in search”, the best change with no
limits and the best change under strict guardrails, each with a predicted effect that is scored later.
One page for the whole archive: all business areas side by side. For each: the share of experiments
that only repeat known results, how fast new knowledge arrives, and advice for the whole organization.
One page per pair of metrics, e.g. exposure and clicks. Does one really drive the other, or did the same
change push both? Tested on clean experiments, where no other intermediate metric moved.
One page per bundle. Several parameters changed at once: which one did the work? Compares the whole
bundle, one parameter tested alone, and the bundle with one parameter removed.
All metric → metric links on one page. Also read backwards: to move this metric, which parameters
Which experiments to run next, ranked by expected gain and by expected information, e.g. two
parameters that were always changed together and never tested alone.
One page per experiment: ship or not, with a grade. Shows the main goal metric and the guardrail
metrics that must not get worse; any guardrail that fires blocks the launch.
One page per business area: is there still room to improve, should we keep investing in experiments
here, and where to bet next?
